clue.text: Thus far successful competitor's forte popular among the top stars

parts.note: f is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud
in, as in 'the in thing', means popular
the A-list is the roster of the biggest celebrities

explanation.surface: A sporting finalist whose strength is being admired by the celebrity elite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has reached the last round has so far won every stage, the deciding match still to come.

clue.text: Fine carpeting beneath one so safe?

indicators.note: beneath in a down entry puts the rebuke below the numeral

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
I is the Roman numeral one
a carpeting is a severe telling-off, a rebuke

explanation.surface: A fine rug laid under something to make it secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpeting' is British for a dressing-down, not floor covering; in a down answer, 'beneath one' places it after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot burn is safe from flames; the question mark marks the narrow sense.

clue.text: Close to temptation, not as chaste?

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word temptation

parts.note: unlike means not as, differing from

explanation.surface: Someone near to giving in to temptation, so not so pure after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Resembling a member of a religious order sworn to celibacy is to be pure, hence the query.

clue.text: Cousin of cricket captain's opening: University's in luck!

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the word for fate

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or luck

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of captain's

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, and the setter keeps the possessive S

explanation.surface: A cricket captain's first innings turns lucky for a university side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cousin of cricket' misleads toward the sport; it is the insect. C, U and the S of 'University's' go inside LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The swarming grasshopper is a close relative of the chirping insect, both in the order Orthoptera.

clue.text: Arab set, perhaps, to provide firm with energy from gas, say

parts.note: stable means firm, steady

indicators.note: from means the energy is taken out of the fuel

parts.note: gas is an example of fuel
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A businesslike plan to give a firm power from gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is a breed of horse, so a set of them fills a stable; E taken from FUEL leaves FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Arab horses are kept in stalls; as many as the building holds is its full complement.

clue.text: Fruit cups selected initially for religious feast

indicators.note: to cup is to hold in cupped hands, so the fruit wraps round the letter

parts.note: a peach is a stone fruit

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word selected is used

explanation.surface: Fruit served in chosen cups for a festive meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' looks like a plural noun (drinking vessels) but is a verb: PEACH holds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesach is the Hebrew name for Passover, the Jewish spring festival with its ritual meal.

clue.text: Pompous official almost to despise in spring uprising

indicators.note: uprising in a down entry means the whole thing reads upward, in reverse
in means the shortened word sits inside the word for jump

parts.note: a hop is a little spring or jump

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to abhor is to despise

explanation.surface: A self-important official nearly scornful of a springtime revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks seasonal but is a jump; 'uprising' in a down answer reads the whole assembly upwards, giving HABHOOP turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: From Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, the Lord High Everything Else, the name now means a self-important functionary.

clue.text: What to see in exotic places, etc?

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A tourist's question about the sights in faraway lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges PLACES ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: A show or display is something to watch, a sight worth looking at.

clue.text: Informal sort of eatery reserves right to do a takeaway

indicators.note: reserves means keeps inside, so the café holds the other letters

parts.note: caff is British slang for a cheap café

explanation.surface: A greasy spoon keeping back food for a takeaway order.
explanation.walkthrough: A caff is a cheap British café. 'takeaway' suggests food to go; here it is removal.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something off on a cart is to remove it, so it is a kind of taking away.

clue.text: As an ineligible candidate you can't beat it!

definitions.text: As an ineligible candidate you can't
definitions.meaning: someone barred from election cannot stand for office
slang for clear off, scarper, flee

explanation.surface: A boast that something is unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you can't beat it' reads as praise, but splits into 'you can't ___' (stand for election) and 'beat it' (flee).
explanation.definitionFit: Standing for office and fleeing are both senses of the one short verb.

clue.text: Driver of old craft circling moon in comfort

indicators.note: in means the craft-and-moon group sits inside the word for comfort

parts.note: to cheer is to comfort or console

indicators.note: circling means the word for craft goes round the moon's name

parts.note: art means craft or skill
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: An old boat sails round the moon in luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text adds a stray 'or' the page does not print. Io is a moon of Jupiter, a crossword favourite; 'circling' and 'in' nest the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient times a two-wheeled war or racing car, drawn by horses, needed a driver of this kind.

clue.text: Father's recited playwright

definitions.note: possessive standing for an adjective: belonging to a Father, a priest

indicators.note: recited means the playwright's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: J. B. Priestley wrote An Inspector Calls

explanation.surface: A dad reciting the work of a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' is a Catholic priest; the adjective for his kind sounds like the surname of the English dramatist J. B. Priestley.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting a cleric: a Father is a priest, so what is the Father's is clerical in character.

clue.text: Mechanical seat

definitions.meaning: Nick ... the weaver is one of the 'rude mechanicals' in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
the part one sits on, the backside

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's weaver among the amateur actors shares his name with the part of the body we sit on.

clue.text: Outstanding description of all those in a singles' bar?

definitions.meaning: unpaid, still due, as a debt

definitions.text: description of all those in a singles' bar?
definitions.meaning: nobody in a bar for single people has a spouse

explanation.surface: A wry comment on the clientele of a bar for single people.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still to be paid is outstanding; the second reading splits the word as zero plus married.

clue.text: Supporter of Charles II wants doctor for treatment

indicators.note: treatment, as of a patient, suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A royalist of King Charles II needs a doctor's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles II' looks like the Stuart king; the Charles is the naturalist, and II joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the theory of evolution by natural selection backs the naturalist Charles of that name.

clue.text: Financial Times's pique about the City being unprepared

parts.note: the possessive read as 'of FT', FT being the abbreviation for the Financial Times

indicators.note: about means the fit of pique goes round the City's letters

parts.note: a huff is a fit of pique
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: The financial paper is annoyed at the Square Mile being caught off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Financial Times's' is read as 'of', giving OF FT. The City is London's financial district, whose postcode letters are EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking without preparation is an idiom from notes jotted on a shirtsleeve, so it means improvised.

clue.text: Method of CID man in hours recalled that of Inspector Clouseau

parts.note: a tec is a detective; the CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department

indicators.note: recalled means the pair of words 'in hours' is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: que is French for that, the language of the French inspector Clouseau

explanation.surface: A detective's way of doing things recalling the bumbling French inspector of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns IN + H into HNI. Clouseau of the Pink Panther films is French, so his 'that' is QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled way of carrying out a task is a procedure or method.

clue.text: Overweight —— so one's pigeon might be working out

parts.note: fat means overweight
a pigeon that finds its way back home is described this way

explanation.surface: A fat man reflecting that his pigeon might be getting exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like exercise for an overweight person; here it means understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to the bottom of a puzzle is to understand it, to solve or figure it out.

clue.text: Officer commanding us in legion for a time

indicators.note: in means the officer phrase sits inside the word for a multitude

parts.note: a legion is a great number, a flock
the officer commanding us is our OC, OC being the military abbreviation for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: An army commander leads our soldiers within a legion for a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer commanding us' is OUR OC, not OC + US, so OUROC goes into FLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Teatime in Britain falls at this hour, which is one particular point on the clock face.

clue.text: Public condemnation he passed on: behold article pinched from wharf

parts.note: ob., short for Latin obiit, he died, is used on memorials
lo is an old word for behold

indicators.note: pinched from means the article is stolen out of the wharf

parts.note: a quay is a wharf
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Censure after a man's death, when an object is stolen from the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched from' removes A from QUAY, leaving QUY.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong public disgrace or censure, abuse heaped on someone, is a formal word for condemnation.

clue.text: Aircraft that comes down on the block?

definitions.text: that comes down on the block?
definitions.meaning: an axe or cleaver brought down on a chopping block or an executioner's block

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a helicopter, and also a cutting tool such as a cleaver or axe that falls on the block.

clue.text: Bridge-player who shortly finishes his game

definitions.text: Bridge-player who shortly finishes his game

parts.words: Bridge-player who shortly finishes his game
parts.note: the four bridge seats are named by compass points; this seat, written short as its initial E, is the final letter of both bridge and game

explanation.surface: A card player who is quick to wrap up the rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' means abbreviated: the seat's one-letter short form is the letter that ends 'bridge' and 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players sit at compass points, and this seat partners West.

clue.text: Style employing frames of amber and tinged with green?

indicators.note: frames of means the outside letters of the words amber and tinged

parts.note: eco- means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: A decorative style using amber frames and a greenish tint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frames of' takes A-R from amber and T-D from tinged; 'green' adds ECO.
explanation.definitionFit: The bold geometric design movement of the 1920s and 30s is a named artistic style.

clue.text: Naval officer went, showing bad form, and danced

parts.note: PO is a Petty Officer in the navy
an ungrammatical past tense of go, as a child might say

explanation.surface: A naval officer behaved badly and took to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad form' means incorrect grammar, so went becomes GOED.
explanation.definitionFit: Punk fans bounced up and down on the spot, a jumping dance named after the spring-loaded stick.

clue.text: Colourless character in England once putting name forward

indicators.note: putting a letter in a new place signals that it moves within the word
forward says the letter shifts nearer the front of the word

parts.note: Albion is an old poetic name for Britain or England

explanation.surface: A pale figure in old England pushing his name ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: In ALBION the N moves forward, ahead of the O.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or animal with no pigment in skin, hair or eyes is pale through lack of colour.

clue.text: A few restored to owner with a love

indicators.note: restored means the letters are put back together in a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A handful of items returned to their rightful owner, along with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges TO OWNER into ONEORTW, then O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, imprecise number is a common idiom for a couple or so.

clue.text: Cash player paid over without question a reward?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the question's letters stand on the outside, ahead of the over

parts.note: a quid is a pound in British slang
a pro is a professional, a paid player
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Money for a professional player, handed over without asking, as a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for a pound. 'without' in its old sense of outside sets the question's letters before the over.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag names something given in return for something else, so a reward or payback fits, with a query.

clue.text: Teacher of Old Testament English moralising at Centre

indicators.note: at Centre means just the middle two letters of the word moralising

explanation.surface: An English Bible teacher preaching at a centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moralising' has ten letters, so its centre is the two letters in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: In the First Book of Samuel the priest at Shiloh raised and instructed the boy Samuel.

clue.text: Regrets you harbour when looking back rather grey

indicators.note: looking back means the run of letters is read from right to left
to harbour is to hold within, so the letters are kept inside the words Regrets you

explanation.surface: Someone nursing regrets while looking back on a dull grey past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' takes RETSYO from inside 'Regrets you'; 'looking back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour name for a pale greyish-white, after the shellfish, so a shade somewhat grey.

clue.text: Poster drawn out by chap in great haste

indicators.note: by means the man's letters stand beside the poster, here at the front

parts.note: he, a male, stands for a chap
an ad, advertisement, is a poster
long means drawn out, protracted

explanation.surface: A man rushing to put up a long notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing recklessly forward, head first, is the idiom for acting with extreme speed and no care.
